findings.evidence: `Histogram1D` and ARCHITECTURE §2/§4.1 call the bin width ``b`` (``b \ll h``, ``O(b^2)``); `density`, `expectation`, `conditional_expectation` and ARCHITECTURE §4.1/§4.B/§11 call it ``\Delta``; `density`, `bandwidth`, `AsymmetricKernel`, `gamma_kernel` and ARCHITECTURE §4.5 use ``b`` for the gamma/beta kernel scale, so ARCHITECTURE alone binds `b` to two concepts. `local_fit` writes ``T_\ell = \sum_j K_h(\ell_j - x) w_j (\ell_j - x)^\ell`` with ℓ as both index and location, and `conditional_expectation_standard_error` then uses ``\ell(x)`` for the leverage. `RULE.DOC.ONE_NOTATION`'s `notation_page` is unset, so it names `docs/src/notation.md`, which does not exist.
findings.claim: The notation is not one-to-one and the package has no notation page to settle it: the bin width is `b` in some places and `Δ` in others while `b` is also the asymmetric-kernel scale; `ℓ` is at once the bin location ℓ_j, the moment index in T_ℓ / P_ℓ (both in one formula of `local_fit`) and the leverage ℓ(x); `w` is the design weight w_j, the effective regression weight w_j(x), the AMISE local-scale weight w(x) and the hyperstatistical mixing weight w_k.
findings.fix: Pick one symbol per concept (e.g. Δ for the bin width everywhere, b reserved for the asymmetric scale; ℓ_j → c̃_j or x_j for locations and k for the moment index; distinct letters for the four weights) and sweep every surface; record the choice on a notation page.
